_doc: Accepted debt for check-element-manifest-conformance.js --check. These numbers may only ever go DOWN. A rise fails the build. Raising one requires a written reason in _accepted below and Bean's sign-off (a new baseline entry is stop-the-line, per Spec 35 / the plan's verification bar).
_promoted: 2026-08-15 — the checker ran WARN-ONLY from its creation. It was promoted to a real gate the same day the D533/D537 placement resolver's last 7 contested attributes were cleared (alignItems, grid-vs-wrapper, on container/cta-section/form/form-field-tiles/hero/pricing-table/tabs). An advisory placement rule is exactly why D537 and D609 drifted into contradicting each other on the record.
_not_gated: total_gap (3363 live) is deliberately NOT gated. A GAP means an element's declared cluster names a CSS property the element has no attribute for — e.g. a container's `fill` cluster naming css:object-fit. That is COVERAGE, not a defect. Gating it would fail every build forever while measuring the wrong thing.

orphan_style_defect.reason: Pre-existing placement defects, present before this gate existed. Not introduced by the promotion. Each needs its own per-block read — they are real, but they are debt to burn down, not a reason to leave the gate off. 2026-08-15: sgs/before-after's 3 (label + divider x2) genuinely fixed — dividerColour/dividerWidth were misattributed to the `divider` element by prefix-string accident and actually paint on a new `divider-line` element; labelBackgroundColour needed `fill` added to the `label` element's clusters. sgs/hero's contentBackgroundGradientFrom (1 of the 2) genuinely fixed via an explicit attrMap entry; contentBackgroundGradientTo remains (no sibling mechanism for a second gradient colour stop). sgs/icon-list's 4 (item-text) also cleared live during this session (SET B's concurrent work on a disjoint block list) and are removed from the instance list below since they are already gone, not because this fix pass touched sgs/icon-list. sgs/testimonial — rating cleared too (resolved elsewhere, unrelated to this session). 2026-08-15 (shadow colour-architecture redesign, D621/D622): sgs/trust-bar's iconCircleShadowColour + badgeImageShadowColour, sgs/team-member's cardShadowColour, and sgs/brand-strip's tileShadowColour are all NEW companion attrs from the same migration — the manifest's `css:box-shadow` cluster member models box-shadow as ONE property (colour included), so it has no vocabulary yet for a colour split OUT of that property into its own attribute (this checker was written before the shadow-colour-split architecture existed). Each shape attr (iconCircleShadow/badgeImageShadow/cardShadow/tileShadow) is still correctly claimed via its own explicit attrMap entry; only the new sibling colour attr has nowhere to register. sgs/card-grid's cardShadowColour/shadowHoverColour and sgs/testimonial's shadowHoverColour are the SAME new companion-attr class but escape this scan entirely (their owning elements declare no explicit `prefix`, or the attr name doesn't start with one), so they never even reach here — not fixed, just invisible to this particular gate; noted for completeness, not counted. Genuinely accepted debt, not a fix regression — extending the manifest vocabulary with a `css:box-shadow-colour` member is future work, tracked separately from this task's shadow-colour-architecture scope. 2026-08-16: sgs/quote's boxShadowColour + boxShadowHoverColour added — the D632 residual block, same companion-attr class, closing the migration's last deferred block. Shape attrs (boxShadow/boxShadowHover) are correctly claimed via the `box` element's attrMap (base + states.hover); only the new sibling colour attrs have nowhere to register, identical to the trust-bar/team-member/brand-strip precedent above. || 2026-08-20 — BURNED DOWN TO ZERO (12 -> 0), Bean-directed. Root-caused as TWO shared-model gaps, not 14 per-block defects: (1) css:box-shadow-color did not exist. box-shadow is a COMPOUND property whose colour half is a separate attribute; it could NOT be another suffix on css:box-shadow because a member claims exactly ONE attribute (the resolver returns on the first matching suffix), so the shadow VALUE always won and every {prefix}ShadowColour in the framework was unclaimable by construction — 8 findings across 6 blocks. Fixed by a sibling member mirroring the css:border-color-gradient precedent, plus 4 explicit attrMap entries for elements that declare no prefix. (2) NO css:outline-* member existed at all, so sgs/form's attrMap entry for css:outline-width pointed at a member that did not exist and could never resolve. Added css:outline-width + css:outline-offset; outline is separately painted and is neither border nor box-shadow. The rest were per-block element/cluster corrections. ⚠ ZERO IS NOW THE FLOOR — this may only go DOWN, and it cannot. Any rise is a genuine new defect: fix it, do not raise this number.

total_state_without_base.reason: 2026-09-05 (process-steps.numberColour HOVER gradient close-out): sgs/process-steps' numberColourHoverGradient added as a new state-only attribute, mirroring the pre-existing hover-only shape of its flat counterpart numberColourHover (the number badge's hover text colour has no resting/base gradient twin by design -- the base numberColour is flat-only) -- same class of gap as sgs/quote's textColourHoverGradient immediately below. Lifted verbatim from sgs/post-grid's textColourHover ancestor-hover pattern per the block's own CLAUDE.md known-precedent registry. 3 -> 4. 2026-09-04 (D948 golden-colour Phase 3, text-colour gradient rollout): sgs/quote's textColourHoverGradient added as a new state-only attribute, mirroring the pre-existing hover-only shape of its flat counterpart textColourHover (quote's hover text colour has no resting/base twin by design) -- same class of gap as the hero/info-box borderColourHoverGradient entries below, a gradient sibling inheriting its flat counterpart's existing state-without-base shape rather than introducing a new kind of defect. 2 -> 3. sgs/post-grid declares a state-scoped css:transform with no resting-state twin. A hover value with nothing to return to is usually a real defect, but it predates this gate and needs a live check before being changed. Second STATE_WITHOUT_BASE on sgs/post-grid, same shape as the existing accepted scaleHover entry — hover-only shadow with no resting-state equivalent is an intentional design choice on this block, not a gap. 2026-08-17 (D636 border-colour gradient sweep, remaining-block batch): sgs/hero's borderColourHoverGradient added as a new state-only attribute. CORRECTED 2026-08-17 (D650/D652) — sgs/hero's wrapper element DOES have a resting border colour: `css:border-color` is claimed at base by native `__experimentalBorder.color` (WordPress's own Border panel), so the resting concept is real and already wired. The gap is narrower than originally stated: WordPress core has never supported a resting-state border GRADIENT, only a resting-state flat colour, so no resting counterpart can exist for this specific gradient attrMap member — that is a WP-core ceiling, not a missing SGS control. The gradient sibling mirrors its flat counterpart's hover-only shape 1:1 for that same reason, not a new defect. Same batch: sgs/info-box's borderColourHoverGradient — same correction applies. The `box` element's base attrMap DOES claim `css:border-color` via native `__experimentalBorder.color`; only `css:border-color-gradient` has no resting counterpart, because WP core has no resting-state border-gradient capability, not because the block lacks a resting border control. || 2026-08-20 — 4 -> 2. sgs/post-grid's shadowHover gap CLOSED by building the missing resting control (new shadow/shadowColour attrs + ShadowControl + render + classification companion), NOT by exempting it. sgs/post-grid's scaleHover reclassified STATE_BY_DESIGN via the new states.<state>.noBaseByDesign declaration — a card's resting scale is 1 by definition, so a 'resting scale' control is clutter not capability (Bean-ruled). The remaining 2 are sgs/hero and sgs/info-box borderColourHoverGradient, HANDED to the colour-golden track (.claude/reports/2026-08-20-HANDOVER-2-to-colour-golden-track.md §1) because closing them is a colour-control mechanism decision. They must be closed by BUILDING the resting control, never by noBaseByDesign. This number may only go DOWN.
